principles.core_question: Are the persons or objects being targeted lawful military objectives?
principles.legal_function: Separates combatants/military objectives from civilians/civilian objects.
principles.common_authorities: Additional Protocol I arts. 48, 51, 52; ICRC Customary IHL Rules 1 and 7
principles.analysis_notes: Start every conduct-of-hostilities analysis with status and object classification.

principles.core_question: Would expected incidental civilian harm be excessive in relation to the concrete and direct military advantage anticipated?
principles.legal_function: Restrains attacks even when the target is military.
principles.common_authorities: Additional Protocol I art. 51(5)(b); ICRC Customary IHL Rule 14
principles.analysis_notes: Do not confuse jus ad bellum proportionality with IHL attack proportionality.

principles.core_question: Were feasible precautions taken to verify targets and minimize civilian harm?
principles.legal_function: Requires planning, verification, warnings where feasible, and choice of means and methods.
principles.common_authorities: Additional Protocol I art. 57; ICRC Customary IHL Rules 15-21
principles.analysis_notes: Evidence often turns on what was feasible based on information available at the time.

principles.core_question: Is the measure directed toward a legitimate military purpose and not otherwise prohibited?
principles.legal_function: Permits only measures necessary to accomplish a legitimate military aim within legal limits.
principles.common_authorities: Hague Regulations; customary IHL; IHL commentaries
principles.analysis_notes: Necessity never authorizes what IHL specifically prohibits.

principles.core_question: Does the conduct avoid unnecessary suffering and protect persons hors de combat?
principles.legal_function: Limits violence through humane treatment, medical protection, and bans on unnecessary suffering.
principles.common_authorities: Common Article 3; Hague principles; Additional Protocol I; customary IHL
principles.analysis_notes: Humanity operates across targeting, detention, medical care, and treatment of persons.

targeting_rules.primary_rule: Civilians may not be made the object of attack.
targeting_rules.required_analysis: Assess status, direct participation, doubt rules, and available intelligence.
targeting_rules.risk_flags: Labeling all military-age males as combatants; weak intelligence; retrospective justification.

targeting_rules.primary_rule: Civilian objects may not be attacked unless they become military objectives.
targeting_rules.required_analysis: Determine nature, location, purpose, or use and contribution to military action.
targeting_rules.risk_flags: Dual-use infrastructure; hospitals; schools; power grids; communications systems.

targeting_rules.primary_rule: Incidental harm must not be excessive relative to concrete and direct military advantage.
targeting_rules.required_analysis: Compare expected civilian casualties and damage with anticipated military advantage.
targeting_rules.risk_flags: Speculative military advantage; aggregated campaign benefits; undercounted civilian presence.

targeting_rules.primary_rule: Effective advance warning must be given where circumstances permit.
targeting_rules.required_analysis: Evaluate feasibility, specificity, timing, safe routes, and actual civilian capacity to comply.
targeting_rules.risk_flags: Evacuation orders without safe destination; siege conditions; disabled or detained populations.

targeting_rules.primary_rule: Weapons and tactics must comply with IHL limits.
targeting_rules.required_analysis: Assess weapon effects, area impact, indiscriminate risks, and special protections.
targeting_rules.risk_flags: Explosive weapons in dense urban areas; autonomous systems; cyber cascading effects.

war_crimes.analysis_notes: Requires analysis of target status, intent/knowledge, and attack context.

war_crimes.conduct: Intentionally directing attacks against civilian objects
war_crimes.analysis_notes: Focuses on whether the object was civilian or had become a military objective.
Requires expected incidental harm and anticipated military advantage analysis.

war_crimes.conduct: Attacks on hospitals or medical units
war_crimes.analysis_notes: Special protection may be lost only under strict conditions after warning where required.

war_crimes.conduct: Impeding humanitarian relief or starvation methods
war_crimes.analysis_notes: Analyze siege, deprivation, consent, access, and civilian survival needs.
